Normalize embeddings X, form A=ReLU(XXᵀ), mask padding pairs, and zero the positional diagonal. Compute C=A.cumsum(dim=-1), so C[b,j,t]=Σₖ≤ₜ,ₖ≠ⱼ max(0,cos(eⱼ,eₖ)). With valid-prefix count nₜ, set sⱼ(t)=C[j,t]/max(nₜ−1,1) for valid j≤t; otherwise zero. Singleton support is zero. Pairwise multiplication costs O(BL²d); cumulative sums cost O(BL²), with O(BL²) storage. A batched multiplication of prefix-specific pooling weights [B,t,j] by embeddings [B,j,d] also costs O(BL²d). This derivation is causal provided embeddings are static item embeddings or causal states, and both pooling and its normalization exclude j>t. Do not triangular-mask A before cumulative summation: an earlier j must include later k once k enters the current prefix.

Evidence favors testing simple pooling seriously, but does not establish this exact positive-cosine recurrence weighting. [HAM](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10034966/) reports recent-window mean pooling outperforming HGN’s learned gates and HAM variants outperforming SASRec on five of six datasets; this is adjacent evidence, not a controlled cosine-versus-recency comparison. [RSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) supports recency-aware training, not recency pooling. Compare identical SASRec residuals using uniform, exponential-recency, support-only, and support×recency weights under matched tuning.

[PAUDRec](https://scholars.cityu.edu.hk/en/publications/popularity-aware-sequential-recommendation-with-user-desire/) documents sequential popularity bias and mitigation across four datasets. [The Unfairness of Popularity Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.13286) shows niche users receiving disproportionately popular recommendations, outside a specifically sequential setting. Inference: support weighting could suppress isolated minority interests by favoring dense similarity clusters; neither source proves that this residual does so. Check long-tail exposure and minority-history retention alongside validation HR@10.
